---
title: "Carrier-resolved local modulation"
---

`audio.modulation.local` describes energy changes jointly by carrier frequency,
temporal rate, spectral scale and spectral direction. It works on a floating-point
mono or multichannel audio mixture. It does not require detected speech, vocals,
beats or a fundamental-frequency track.

```python
from natural_features.core.stimulus import AudioStimulus
from natural_features.features.audio import local_spectrotemporal_modulation

features = local_spectrotemporal_modulation(
    AudioStimulus(samples, 16000),
    carriers_hz=[125., 250., 500., 1000., 2000., 4000.],
    rates_hz=[2., 4., 8., 16.],
    scales_cpo=[0.5, 1., 2.],
)
```

The output dimensions are
`(time, carrier_hz, rate_hz, scale_cpo, spectral_sign)`. Positive spectral sign
with positive temporal rate describes downward constant-phase contours. The
values are absolute complex Gabor responses to log10 power, with zero-DC,
unit-L2 spectral and temporal kernels. They are not loudness, a transcription,
or a physiological auditory-model prediction.

The frontend uses complete periodic-Hann FFT-power frames, 64 triangular ERB
bands and interpolation onto a uniform log2-frequency grid. Channels are
averaged. Frequency limits and modulation Nyquist limits are checked; extraction
does not silently resample audio or reduce the requested frequency range.

## Native clocks and support

The default frontend hop is 10 ms, frontend frame 25 ms, filter window 2 s and
output hop 100 ms. Parameters are rounded to actual sample/frame counts and both
requested settings and effective values are recorded. With these defaults, a
filter output depends on **2.015 s of waveform**, because 200 overlapping frames
include the final frame's full 25 ms input.

- `times_s` gives the availability endpoint of each complete filter output.
- `time_bounds_s` gives nonoverlapping output-hop observation cells ending at
  those times. These are the cells for time-weighted aggregation.
- `metadata["computation_context"]["dependency_bounds_s"]` separately gives each
  output's full waveform dependency. These longer intervals must not be
  mistaken for independent observation cells.

Only complete windows are returned; there is no padding. The initial warm-up is
unavailable output, not zero modulation evidence. Cropping input before extraction
changes available context. The consuming analysis chooses target windows and
pooling and must disclose both observation coverage and input dependencies.

## Qualification and limits

Tests cover known carrier/rate/scale/direction preference, time reversal,
constant/log-offset invariance, independent direct filter calculations, finite
silence, append/future independence, offsets, stereo averaging, complete
parameter hashes and the public registry. The log-power floor means gain
invariance should only be expected where a gain change acts as a uniform log
power offset; no claim of invariance across floor crossings is made.

This is a deterministic signal descriptor. Synthetic qualification does not
establish physiological equivalence or neural selectivity. The frequency
frontend, taper, amplitudes, axes, support and provenance remain explicit so a
consumer can test those separate questions.
